newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Unwinding, hedging dominate trade.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Unwinding, hedging dominate trade.

text.p: Unwinding of existing positions and protection-oriented strategies dominated U.S. equity options activity on Monday, traders said.
Despite a fairly strong rally in the stock market overall since Friday, investors were still very cautious that the worst might not be over after recent declines, they said.

"There's still caution out there. We get more request for hedging strategies than anything else," said Michael Schwartz, a managing director of Oppenheimer & Co. "But they're not selling out, they're just looking for ways to protect."
Popular strategies included selling calls against stock positions, using index puts against a portfolio of stocks, and various types of spreads, Schwartz said.

Rod Jamieson, vice president of option strategies at EVEREN Securities, agreed that there was little directional bias in order flows today, adding that most of the actively traded options were the usual technology names.
"Some people who were fortunate enough to buy stocks last week were selling some calls," he said. "But it wasn't big, it's just been a mixed day, no bias one way or another."
A brokerage trader said big volume in many in-the-money options indicated a lot of position unwinding was taking place.

For instance, he said, Cisco Systems Inc April 50.0 call topped the Chicago Board Options Exchange (CBOE) most actives list with 5,564 contracts trading by mid-afternoon. The stock was up 3-1/4 at 54-1/8 after news of an expansion in the firm's computer networking product line.
Cisco's April 55.0 calls and April 50.0 puts also had turnover of more than 3,000 contracts each.

Among other heavily traded contracts, Office Depot Inc options continued trading heavily, most notably in in-the-money puts, in the aftermath of last Friday's Federal Trade Commission (FTC) vote against a revamped merger between Office Depot and Staples Inc.
With the stock price up 1 to 14 in mid-afternoon business, April 15.0 and 17.5 puts traded 11,584 and 6,202 contracts respectively on the American Stock Exchange (AMEX).
"Most likely, these were puts held by arbitrageurs," Schwartz at Oppenheimer noted. "If arbitrageurs are getting out, then the deal must really be over."
Staples April 20.0 and June 30.0 puts were also among the most actives on the Philadelphia Stock Exchange, with volume of 1,880 and 1,140 contracts respectively. The stock was up 3/4 at 22-5/8.
Traders on AMEX floor had said on Friday that the high level of activity in Office Depot puts after the news on the FTC vote was due mainly to professional institutions.
